claims.text: Elevated-temperature anomalies in HfNbTaTiZr stress–strain response, thermal expansion, and elastic moduli arise from local lattice distortion combined with anharmonic lattice vibrations.
Atomic-size mismatch and high mixing entropy produce pronounced local lattice distortions in HfNbTaTiZr.
At moderate elevated temperatures, the heterogeneous energy landscape associated with lattice distortion strongly impedes thermally activated dislocation glide.
Impeded dislocation glide produces an increased effective yield stress at moderate temperatures.
At higher temperatures, increased lattice anharmonicity accelerates thermal expansion.
At higher temperatures, anharmonic lattice vibrations soften the elastic moduli faster than predicted by simple harmonic models.
Elevated-temperature atomic vibrations promote dynamic recovery, including dislocation climb, and reduce dislocation density.
Dynamic recovery partially softens the elevated-temperature stress response.
Relative to room-temperature HfNbTaTiZr, the alloy will initially exhibit increased yield stress at moderate temperatures and pronounced softening at higher temperatures.
HfNbTaTiZr will exhibit a non-linear stress–strain response over the tested elevated-temperature range.
The thermal expansion coefficient of HfNbTaTiZr will deviate increasingly upward from linear or harmonic predictions as temperature rises.
The elastic moduli of HfNbTaTiZr will decrease more precipitously with temperature than those of a simpler refractory-alloy control.
A simpler refractory alloy such as binary Hf–Nb has lower local lattice distortion than HfNbTaTiZr.
The proposed responses remain qualitatively robust despite uncertainty in their magnitudes.
The proposed mechanism applies only while HfNbTaTiZr remains single-phase and oxidation and phase transformations are absent.
Below the onset of rapid recovery, thermally activated dislocation glide is the primary deformation mechanism and diffusion-mediated creep is minimal.
